heading: Cold open
narration: A quenched knife and a soft nail both cling to the same magnet.

heading: Cold open
narration: The dependable way to tell if steel is hardened is to measure its resistance to indentation, most often with a Rockwell C test that presses a diamond cone into the surface under 150 kilograms-force, a method standardized by ASTM International.

heading: Cold open
narration: That number settles one thing well: how hard the steel is at one small spot near the surface.

heading: Cold open
narration: It does not settle how deep the hardness runs. It does not show whether the part was tempered afterwards, or whether the steel a few centimetres away behaved the same way in the quench.

heading: Cold open
narration: Each of those needs its own kind of evidence. The cheap shop tests you may have heard of answer different questions again.

heading: Title card
narration: How to tell if steel is hardened

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: Start with what hardening physically does. Carbon steel is iron with a small fraction of carbon dissolved in it.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: Heat it past 727 degrees Celsius, the eutectoid temperature on the iron-carbon phase diagram, and the iron reorganizes into a crystal structure called austenite, which can hold much more carbon in solution.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: For many steels the hardening temperature sits somewhat above that line. The exact figure depends on the alloy, so a heat treater reads it from the data for that grade rather than from memory.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: Cool the steel slowly and the carbon has time to migrate out, forming softer, layered structures.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: Quench it fast, in water, brine or oil, and the carbon is trapped where it sits.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: The iron lattice tries to shift back to its room-temperature arrangement anyway. What results is a strained, distorted crystal called martensite.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: Martensite is what a hardened part is mostly made of, and it is why this question is harder than it sounds.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: ASM International's heat-treating references describe martensite as hard and brittle as quenched.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: That is why nearly every hardened tool is tempered afterwards: reheated to a moderate temperature to give up some hardness in exchange for toughness.

args.meaning: the strained crystal that forms when quenching traps carbon in iron
args.boundary: hard and brittle as quenched, so it is tempered

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: None of this announces itself on the surface. A quenched blade keeps its shape, looks much the same once cleaned, and carries no visible label.

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: Every practical test is therefore an indirect measurement of a structure you cannot see.

args.meaning: the strained crystal that forms when quenching traps carbon in iron
args.boundary: hard and brittle as quenched, so it is tempered

heading: Hardening rearranges the inside and leaves the outside alone
narration: The useful habit is to ask, for each test, which property of that structure it actually touches.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: The magnet is the most common shortcut, and it fails for a simple reason.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: Ordinary carbon steel is ferromagnetic whether it is soft, annealed or fully hardened, so the knife and the nail both pass.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: The magnet cannot tell you about heat treatment at all. What it does respond to is the family of crystal structure.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: Many austenitic stainless steels, the kind used for kitchen sinks, are essentially non-magnetic in the annealed state, and they also cannot be hardened by quenching.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: Martensitic stainless grades, used for many knife blades, are magnetic. So a magnet can sometimes hint at whether a steel is the kind that could be hardened. It says nothing about whether anyone has done it.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: Temper colours are the second shortcut. When bright steel is heated in air, a thin oxide film grows on it.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: The film's thickness depends on temperature and time, and it produces colours running from pale straw through bronze and purple to blue.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: Smiths have long used those colours to judge tempering. But read carefully what they record: the surface was heated in air to some temperature.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: They do not show that the steel was quenched first, since soft mild steel colours the same way.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: And because time matters as well as temperature, a colour alone cannot tell you how hard the steel is now.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: Grinding or polishing removes the film entirely. The spark test, where a grinding wheel throws sparks whose bursts reflect carbon content, has the same character.

heading: A magnet and a temper colour are answering other questions
narration: It suggests whether a steel could be hardened, not whether it has been.

heading: Producer POV
narration: Once I can locate the failure — bad source, lazy assumption, missing context, evidence I ignored because it was inconvenient — I can let the belief go.

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: The file test is the oldest honest shortcut, because it actually tests hardness.

args.title: File test
steps: Draw it lightly across a clean edge
Feel whether it bites or skids

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: A file is itself made of hardened steel. Choose a sharp file, draw it lightly across a clean edge of the part, and feel whether it bites or skids.

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: If it bites, cutting bright metal with a slight drag, the part is softer than the file.

args.title: File test
steps: Draw it lightly across a clean edge
Feel whether it bites or skids

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: If it skids across with a glassy feel and leaves almost no mark, the part is about as hard as the file, or harder.

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: Industry still uses this as a screening check. Sets of files made to graded hardness exist, so that the skid point can be bracketed more closely.

args.title: File test
steps: Draw it lightly across a clean edge
Feel whether it bites or skids

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: But notice what the file is touching: the outermost skin, and only where you dragged it.

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: Two common situations break the inference. A case-hardened part, such as a carburized gear, has a hard shell over a deliberately softer core.

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: The file skids, correctly, yet the core may be far softer than the skid suggests.

excludes: evidence the whole part is hard

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: The reverse happens with decarburization, when carbon is lost from the surface during heating in air.

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: The skin turns soft while the interior stays hard, and the file bites a part that is, underneath, properly hardened.

excludes: evidence the whole part is hard

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: The result also depends on the file's sharpness and the pressure of your hand.

heading: A file ranks hardness by whether it can cut
narration: So it ranks the surface only, and it ranks it against the file you happen to hold.

excludes: evidence the whole part is hard

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: The Rockwell C test replaces the hand with a machine and the feel with a depth.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: A diamond cone with a 120-degree tip is first pressed against the surface with a 10 kilograms-force preload.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: That seats the indenter and sets a zero below any surface roughness.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: Then the load rises to 150 kilograms-force total, is held briefly, and is reduced back to the preload.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: The machine records the depth difference between the two preload readings: how much permanent dent the full load left.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: A harder steel resists, the dent is shallower, and the Rockwell C number is higher.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: On this scale each point corresponds to two thousandths of a millimetre of depth.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: That is why the reading is so sensitive to dirt, scale and vibration.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: ASTM International sets out the procedure in its standard for Rockwell testing of metallic materials, designated E18.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: It specifies the indenter, the forces, the dwell times, and rules a non-specialist would not think to ask about.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: The test piece must be thick enough that the dent does not reach the far side, or the anvil underneath is partly being measured.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: Indentations must be spaced away from edges and from each other, because each one disturbs the metal around it.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: Curved surfaces, like round bars, need corrections, because a cone sinks differently into a curve.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: A Rockwell number taken without those conditions met is a number, but not yet evidence.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: Other methods trade convenience for different strengths. The Brinell test presses a hard ball into the metal and measures the width of the round impression, which averages over coarser structures but leaves a large mark.

includes: a measured diagonal of a square diamond dent

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: The Vickers test uses a square-based diamond pyramid and measures the diagonals of the dent under a microscope.

heading: A Rockwell number is a depth, read twice
narration: With small loads it can place indentations a fraction of a millimetre apart, which matters for a question the file could never answer.

includes: a measured diagonal of a square diamond dent

heading: A hardness number is only as good as the block behind it
narration: Here is the part of the chain most people never see. A hardness tester does not measure an absolute physical quantity the way a ruler measures length.

heading: A hardness number is only as good as the block behind it
narration: The number depends on the exact geometry of the diamond, the accuracy of the forces, and the depth sensor.

heading: A hardness number is only as good as the block behind it
narration: Two machines that differ slightly in any of those will disagree. So machines are checked against reference test blocks: pieces of steel prepared to be uniform and certified at a known hardness.

heading: A hardness number is only as good as the block behind it
narration: NIST produces Rockwell C reference test blocks, calibrated on its own standardizing equipment, and the ASTM International standard specifies how machines are verified against blocks.

heading: A hardness number is only as good as the block behind it
narration: When a lab reports a hardness, the defensible claim is that the machine read a certified block correctly that day, and then read your part.

args.title: Reference blocks
sources: produces Rockwell C reference test blocks

heading: A hardness number is only as good as the block behind it
narration: That traceability is what turns the file's private judgement into a public measurement.

heading: A hardness number is only as good as the block behind it
narration: Your hand cannot be sent to another laboratory. A certified block can.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: Hardness tells you how much the metal resists; the microscope tells you why.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: A metallographer cuts a cross-section through the part, mounting it and polishing it flat, then gives it a nital etch.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: Nital is a dilute solution of nitric acid in alcohol. The acid attacks different structures at different rates, so the grain pattern appears.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: Under a microscope, properly hardened steel shows martensite, which looks needle-like or lath-like, fine and dense.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: Slowly cooled steel shows rounded grains and layered bands instead. Soft spots, where the quench was too slow, show up as patches of the wrong structure.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: The same section answers the depth question the file could not. Run a line of small Vickers or Knoop indentations from the surface inward, and you get a hardness profile.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: On a case-hardened gear the numbers start high and fall off with depth.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: The depth at which they cross an agreed threshold is reported as the case depth.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: ASTM International publishes the microindentation method used for this kind of traverse.

heading: A cross-section shows why the number is high
narration: The cost is obvious: the part has been cut in half. In production, that is why a test coupon, or a sacrificial part from the same batch, carries the destructive evidence for the rest.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: As you watch, notice where each diagram ends. The file test ranks the surface.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: The Rockwell C test measures a depth at one point, traced back to a certified block.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: Nothing in this episode shows that the magnet test detects hardening, which is why it never earns a place on the hardened side.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: And case depth needs a cross-section, which means some of the most important evidence about a hardened part is gathered on a different, destroyed piece of the same batch.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: The tests are not ranked from crude to good. Each one is matched to a narrower question than it first appears to answer.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: A hardness reading does not establish that a part is fit for its job.

includes: resistance to one indenter under one load

heading: Evidence limit
narration: It measures resistance to one indenter under one load at one spot.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: It does not measure toughness, so a part can read high and still crack in service if it was left untempered or tempered badly.

includes: resistance to one indenter under one load

heading: Evidence limit
narration: It does not directly measure wear life or fatigue strength, which depend on structure, residual stress and surface finish as well.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Conversions between Rockwell, Vickers and Brinell numbers come from published tables that are empirical and approximate, so a converted value is weaker evidence than a direct one.

includes: resistance to one indenter under one load

heading: Evidence limit
narration: And none of these tests, alone, tells you the heat-treatment history that produced the result.

heading: Closing
narration: So the knife and the nail are told apart by a dent, not by a magnet: a dent of a known depth, under a known force, from a machine that read a certified block that morning.

heading: Closing
narration: Everything you want to say beyond that spot, you have to go and measure.
